flashcards.back: A form of software testing by which isolated source code is tested to validate expected behavior.
flashcards.quote: Unit testing, also known as component or module testing, is a form of software testing by which isolated source code is tested to validate expected behavior.

quizQuestions.question: What does unit testing validate?
options: Expected behavior of isolated source code
quizQuestions.quote: Unit testing, also known as component or module testing, is a form of software testing by which isolated source code is tested to validate expected behavior.

flashcards.front: What does a test case specify?
flashcards.back: The inputs, execution conditions, testing procedure, and expected results for a single test.
flashcards.quote: a test case is a specification of the inputs, execution conditions, testing procedure, and expected results

quizQuestions.question: What does a test case specify?
options: The color of the test report
Inputs, execution conditions, procedure, and expected results
quizQuestions.quote: a test case is a specification of the inputs, execution conditions, testing procedure, and expected results

flashcards.front: When are unit tests written in test-driven development?
flashcards.back: Before the related production code is written.
flashcards.quote: In test-driven development (TDD), unit tests are written before the related production code is written.

quizQuestions.question: In TDD, when are unit tests written?
quizQuestions.quote: In test-driven development (TDD), unit tests are written before the related production code is written.

flashcards.back: Software that satisfies a dependency so the test need not depend on production code.
flashcards.quote: A test double is software used in software test automation that satisfies a dependency so that the test need not depend on production code.

quizQuestions.question: Why use a test double?
options: To speed up compilation of the release
So the test need not depend on production code
quizQuestions.quote: A test double is software used in software test automation that satisfies a dependency so that the test need not depend on production code.

flashcards.back: A test that accepts a set of values so it can run with multiple, different input values.
flashcards.quote: A parameterized test is a test that accepts a set of values that can be used to enable the test to run with multiple, different input values.

quizQuestions.question: What can parameterized tests reduce?
quizQuestions.quote: Use of parametrized tests can reduce test code duplication.

flashcards.front: Why can testing not catch every error in a program?
flashcards.back: It cannot evaluate every execution path in any but the most trivial programs.
flashcards.quote: Testing will not catch every error in the program, because it cannot evaluate every execution path in any but the most trivial programs.

quizQuestions.question: Will unit testing by definition catch integration errors?
options: No, it will not catch them
quizQuestions.quote: Therefore, it will not catch integration errors or broader system-level errors

summaryPoints.text: Unit testing is a form of software testing that checks isolated source code to validate expected behavior.
summaryPoints.quote: Unit testing, also known as component or module testing, is a form of software testing by which isolated source code is tested to validate expected behavior.

summaryPoints.text: Unit tests run at the unit level, in contrast to testing at the integration or system level.
summaryPoints.quote: Unit testing describes tests that are run at the unit-level to contrast testing at the integration or system level.

summaryPoints.text: A test case specifies the inputs, execution conditions, procedure, and expected results for one test.
summaryPoints.quote: a test case is a specification of the inputs, execution conditions, testing procedure, and expected results

summaryPoints.text: In test-driven development, unit tests are written before the related production code.
summaryPoints.quote: In test-driven development (TDD), unit tests are written before the related production code is written.

summaryPoints.text: A parameterized test runs with multiple input values and can reduce test code duplication.
summaryPoints.quote: Use of parametrized tests can reduce test code duplication.

summaryPoints.text: Testing cannot catch every error, and unit testing will not catch integration or system-level errors.
summaryPoints.quote: Therefore, it will not catch integration errors or broader system-level errors
